title.en: Describe pyramids of number, biomass and energy
State the limitations of ecological pyramids

say.en: Count the insects on one big banyan tree and you get a pyramid standing on its tip. Weigh the life in the sea and the same thing happens. But energy never turns upside down. In this lesson: Describe pyramids of number, biomass and energy.
Explain inverted pyramids with examples.
State the limitations of ecological pyramids.

body.en: The relationship between trophic levels can be shown as a *pyramid* in terms of number, biomass or energy. The base of each pyramid represents the producers (first trophic level) and the apex the top-level consumers. In most ecosystems all the pyramids are upright: producers are more in number and biomass than herbivores, and herbivores more than carnivores; energy at a lower trophic level is always more than at a higher level. In a grassland pyramid of numbers (NCERT data), producers number 5,842,424, primary consumers 708,624, secondary consumers 354,904 and tertiary consumers only 3. When calculating these, all organisms at a trophic level must be included, not just a few individuals.

narration.en: Ecological pyramids show numbers, biomass or energy at each trophic level, with producers at the base. In most ecosystems they are upright: a grassland has millions of plants, hundreds of thousands of herbivores and only three top carnivores.
narration.kn: ಪರಿಸರೀಯ ಪಿರಮಿಡ್‌ಗಳು ಪ್ರತಿ ಪೋಷಣಾ ಹಂತದ ಸಂಖ್ಯೆ, ಜೀವರಾಶಿ ಅಥವಾ ಶಕ್ತಿಯನ್ನು ತೋರಿಸುತ್ತವೆ; ತಳದಲ್ಲಿ ಉತ್ಪಾದಕಗಳು. ಹೆಚ್ಚಿನ ಪರಿಸರ ವ್ಯವಸ್ಥೆಗಳಲ್ಲಿ ಅವು ನೇರ: ಹುಲ್ಲುಗಾವಲಿನಲ್ಲಿ ಲಕ್ಷಾಂತರ ಸಸ್ಯಗಳು, ಸಾವಿರಾರು ಸಸ್ಯಾಹಾರಿಗಳು ಮತ್ತು ಕೇವಲ ಮೂರು ಉನ್ನತ ಮಾಂಸಾಹಾರಿಗಳು.

say.en: Base: producers; apex: top consumers.
Grassland numbers: 5,842,424 gives 708,624 gives 354,904 gives 3.
Most pyramids are upright.
Stack the trophic levels as bars, producers at the base. The pyramid of energy is always upright, because energy is lost at every step.
A grassland pyramid of numbers is upright too: millions of grass plants support just three top carnivores.
In the sea, the pyramid of biomass is inverted: a small standing crop of fast-growing phytoplankton supports a larger biomass of consumers.
Pyramids have limits: a species may feed at two levels, real food webs are ignored, and saprophytes are left out.

body.en: Some pyramids are *inverted*. The pyramid of numbers is inverted when a very large number of insects feed on a single big tree: one producer supports thousands of consumers. The pyramid of biomass in the sea is generally inverted, because the biomass of fishes far exceeds that of the phytoplankton. The pyramid of energy is always upright and can never be inverted, because when energy flows from one trophic level to the next some energy is always lost as heat at each step; each bar of the energy pyramid shows the amount of energy at each trophic level in a given time or annually per unit area. Ecological pyramids have limitations: they do not take into account the same species belonging to two or more trophic levels; they assume a simple food chain, which almost never exists in nature, and do not accommodate a food web; and saprophytes are not given any place in them, even though they play a vital role in the ecosystem.

points.en: *Inverted* pyramid of numbers: insects on a big tree
*Inverted* pyramid of biomass: sea (fish biomass > phytoplankton)
*Limitations*: species at two levels, no food web, no saprophytes

problem.en: For each case say whether the pyramid is upright or inverted: (a) pyramid of numbers for grass → grasshopper → frog → snake; (b) pyramid of biomass in the ocean; (c) pyramid of energy in the ocean; (d) pyramid of numbers for a banyan tree → insects.

steps.en: (a) Many grass plants, fewer grasshoppers, fewer frogs, fewest snakes: upright.
(b) Fish biomass far exceeds phytoplankton biomass at a given time: inverted.
(c) Energy is lost at every transfer, so energy pyramids are always upright.
(d) One tree supports thousands of insects: inverted.

say.en: Let us work through this together. For each case say whether the pyramid is upright or inverted: a pyramid of numbers for grass gives grasshopper gives frog gives snake; b pyramid of biomass in the ocean; c pyramid of energy in the ocean; d pyramid of numbers for a banyan tree gives insects.
a Many grass plants, fewer grasshoppers, fewer frogs, fewest snakes: upright.
b Fish biomass far exceeds phytoplankton biomass at a given time: inverted.
c Energy is lost at every transfer, so energy pyramids are always upright.
d One tree supports thousands of insects: inverted.
So the answer is a upright; b inverted; c upright; d inverted.
